podcast.body: This album further explored Talking Heads' "nationwide status" and was "awash in kitschy Americana." It was powered by a string of radio singles, none of which cracked the pop Top 40, but all became staples on album rock radio, and their "cutting-edge videos" were popular on MTV. Hits included "Road to Nowhere" (number 25 rock radio), "The Perky and She Was" (number 11 rock chart, number 54 Hot 100 with a 20-week run), and "Stay Up Late" (number 24 rock radio). "1985's Little Creatures was powered by a string of radio singles."
